summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.3U (Real Runtime Dispatch Authority and Permission Contract Architecture) is a read-only architecture/contract-design phase that made the two decisions Phase 3T deliberately deferred. Re-derived RPAC-REQ-044/045/046 exact wording from docs/contracts/RUNTIME_PROVIDER_ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md (unchanged since 3T) and their exact, non-overreaching responsibilities. Reconstructed the current PermissionBrokerRequest field set and PB action_type/execution_class vocabulary from src/pcae/core/permission_broker_foundation.py, confirming RPAC-REQ-044's insufficiency claim directly. Determined POL-005 is an invariant condition tied to the missing COMP-002 execution boundary, not a permanent universal deny, and is not modified by this phase. Decomposed real dispatch into 6 separable effects (adapter invocation, process spawn, network egress, provider request, filesystem mutation, credential use) and assigned each to its correct owner (PB, Shell Gate, a future network mechanism, adapter implementation, existing mutation actions, a future credential architecture respectively), avoiding overloading PB. Evaluated 3 PB redesign options (dedicated action; mode-enum-on-existing-action; composite per-effect permissions) against 9 criteria in Matrix B and selected Option A (dedicated runtime_dispatch action) for its combination of high semantic clarity, low authority-conflation risk, and narrow PB scope consistent with RPAC-REQ-085. Defined the minimum PB request binding (12 immutable facts, each individually justified, Matrix C columns 1-2) with explicit exclusions (raw credentials, universal provider/model fields, mandatory budget fields for v1). Reconstructed the full human-authority universe (CHGR-001, Interactive Workflow Confirmation, approval_present field, phase/task lifecycle, AESIC, legacy CLI approval flags) into Matrix A, confirming none authorizes real runtime invocation today. Re-confirmed RWMPC-REQ-023's Confirmation-is-not-approval wall unweakened. Defined human runtime-authority requirements (who/what invocation/which target/which repo-task/which prompt hash/which capability class/freshness/one-shot-or-reusable/revocation) and evaluated 3 authority options, selecting Option A (dedicated, one-shot RuntimeInvocationApproval artifact) over Option B (CHGR extension, rejected because CHGR's own README disclaims authority resolution) and Option C (phase/session approval, rejected as too coarse). Defined the exact subject-binding five-tuple, the full freshness/invalidation set (7 mandatory-for-v1 items, none deferred), storage in the .pcae canonical governance store pattern (not CHGR, not the invocation record directly), and trust mechanisms (schema validation, subject binding, provenance, tamper detection reused from existing CHGR-adjacent patterns, no signature required for v1). Designed the approval creation and consumption paths and the PB/authority relationship: PB independently validates a reference, never receives the raw artifact or a caller-supplied approved boolean. Froze the 11-gate ordering (prompt -> target selection -> static preflight -> human authority creation -> approval validation -> Permission Broker -> Runtime Enforcement -> process/network containment -> durable pre-dispatch record -> adapter dispatch -> result capture/intake) as Matrix D, with each ordering choice justified against RPAC-REQ-045/047 and failure-before-effect economics. Confirmed capability-before-authority (static preflight before human approval, live preflight re-checked immediately before dispatch) and PB-before-Runtime-Enforcement (matching RPAC-REQ-045's literal text). Defined the exact Runtime Enforcement handoff projection, explicitly guarding against inferring authority from PB ALLOW alone or approval alone. Mapped the new gates onto the existing Execution Attempt Boundary contract (Phase 99) without redefining it. Defined invocation-record binding by reference/hash (not duplication) and the durable-before-effect minimum set (8 items). Produced the TOCTOU model (Matrix E: 7 mutable facts, each classified snapshot-bound vs. freshly-re-checked-before-dispatch) and canonical prompt-hash semantics (semantic content only, not unstable formatting/environment metadata). Defined repository binding (git-derived fingerprint, not path), task/session/phase binding (session bound only when session-scoped), runtime-target binding (exact, no fallback), adapter descriptor binding (identity only at approval time, version/hash pinning deferred to preflight), and provider/model binding (mandatory for API targets only, never universal). Verified the exact PB outcome vocabulary (ALLOW/DENY/HUMAN_REVIEW, DENY > HUMAN_REVIEW > ALLOW precedence) directly from source and resolved the mandatory HUMAN_REVIEW question with direct evidence: POL-004 (MissingHumanApprovalRule) already resolves HUMAN_REVIEW to not-triggered exactly when a valid RuntimeInvocationApproval sets approval_present=True -- no additional review layer, no policy escalation, no cross-request reuse is invented; this closes Step 39/40 without guessing. Confirmed simulation-path compatibility (the dry consumer's simulation_only=True path is entirely untouched, additive-only design) and backward compatibility (rollback/push/publication/mutation-root actions untouched). Defined policy-versioning (Runtime Enforcement must not cache a decision across a policy-version change) and authority-versioning (additive-evolution discipline matching CHGR/CLTR precedent). Selected approval consumption timing at the same durable 'dispatch attempted' write that marks the effect boundary, after analyzing 4 candidate consumption points and their crash windows (Matrix-adjacent analysis), and defined crash-before-dispatch and crash-after-dispatch recovery semantics, both requiring fresh authorization on retry (no automatic replay, per RPAC-REQ-072). Restricted v1 to one bounded external dispatch per invocation (no multi-effect). Specialized the local-CLI v1 field set (no network field required true, no credential fields) and documented the API-provider extension path as strictly additive and out of v1 scope. Explicitly flagged network-egress permission as an unresolved open dependency (Step 52-54), assigned to neither PB nor this phase, deferred to a future dedicated architecture phase. Distinguished filesystem-mutation authority (existing, unmodified mutation actions) and process/shell authority (Shell Gate or equivalent, independently constrained, unaffected by any PB runtime_dispatch grant) from the new dispatch permission. Recovered both 3S.2.1 MUST-FIX findings verbatim again and reconfirmed their disposition unchanged by this architecture (neither made reachable, neither repaired). Reconfirmed the runtime-inspect TRUTHFUL_WITH_LIMITATION disposition unchanged (still repair before first real adapter). Produced the authority threat model, permission threat model, and cross-gate threat model (Step 57-59), each of the three named cross-gate confusions made structurally impossible by construction. Produced Matrix F (10 security invariants, each with existing control and missing control columns). Assessed and rejected a combined authority/permission artifact (different lifecycles, different provenance, different trust boundaries -- separate provenance with linkage preferred). Recommended 4 future contract artifacts (Runtime Invocation Human Authority Contract; PB Runtime Dispatch Extension Contract; Dispatch Gate Ordering Contract; invocation authority schema) without prematurely freezing any of them. Reached a split contract-freeze verdict: Outcome A (ready to freeze) for the local-CLI-only v1 path, Outcome B (one more architecture-clarification phase needed) for the API-provider path, justified directly from 3T's own finding that local CLI has strictly fewer unique blockers. Derived the implementation dependency order for a future phase (authority artifact -> PB request/policy support -> approval-validation logic -> independent verification -> Runtime Enforcement integration -> Shell Gate/local-CLI chain, converging at the first real adapter) and stated the first-implementation-stop guardrail explicitly: authority/PB implementation alone does not make real execution available. 0 production src/pcae or tests files modified. Execution activated: NO. External runtime invocation: NONE. No PB action implemented. No authority artifact created. No policy changed. Real-runtime readiness: NO, unchanged. Runtime remains Observed/observe/unavailable throughout; v0.4.3 unchanged. Article STOPPED; private research repository untouched. Human decision required before any further work.
